title: Onboarding profile publisher and sampling adapters for deterministic model performance generation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Model onboarding lacks a deterministic, auditable path from eval harness output to published performance profile. Current profile generation is ad-hoc: datasets and sampled prompts are not consistently captured; eval runners differ in metadata emitted; and model version pinning between the harness and catalog is manual. This makes rollouts and perf regressions hard to reproduce.

Goal: Extend the benchmark harness to produce reproducible performance profiles that can be published to the model catalog automatically. Deliverables: (1) sampling adapters that implement deterministic seeding and record sampling provenance (dataset id, seed, sample strategy, filters), (2) an immutable profile publisher that packages evaluation artifacts (raw outputs, metrics, sampled prompts) with a profile manifest (schema v1) and (3) a lightweight version pinning flow that writes the runtime-compatible model variant tags into the manifest for consumption by serving and rollout tooling.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can re-run any published profile and get identical summary metrics within defined floating-point tolerances.
- Profile manifest includes dataset provenance, prompt snippets, seed, eval runner version, harness git SHA, and recommended runtime pin (model:variant:quant).
- Publishing step creates an artifact in the profile registry (S3 + catalog index entry) and a referenceable model-profile id.
- CI verifies end-to-end: run small smoke eval -> publish -> fetch -> re-run -> compare metrics.

Non-goals: Changing model evaluation metrics themselves, rewriting the entire harness. This work focuses on adapters, metadata, and publisher glue.

Risks & trade-offs: Deterministic sampling increases effort for very large corpora (we will provide stratified reservoir sampling adapters that stream). Adding extra artifacts increases storage costs (we propose TTL for raw outputs after 90 days). Pinning versions in manifests can delay adoption if we are too conservative; recommend including both recommended pins and fallback families.

Design notes: Use a manifest JSON line schema (flat top-level keys) so downstream systems (catalog, console) can ingest without nested decoders. Manifest fields: profile_id, created_at, harness_sha, eval_runner, dataset_id, sample_strategy, seed, sample_size, model_recommendation, metrics_summary_link, artifacts_bucket_path. See design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Model+Profile+Publisher (internal).
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes posted to the design doc. Defined initial manifest fields and storage location (s3://redwood-profiles/staging). Asked infra team for temporary write creds.

2026-02-18 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented deterministic sampling adapter (stratified-reservoir). Local unit tests pass for small datasets. Pushed initial WIP branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/1123
2026-02-23 - Design review (Dana Lee): Recommend including prompt canonicalization ID and a short-hash of the prompt template to speed diffs in console. Added to manifest schema.

2026-02-27 - Marco Ruiz: CI flaky test found: hash mismatch on floating-point metrics between Python and Rust evaluation runners. Narrowed to differences in aggregator order. Introducing a stable reducer with explicit sort by prompt-id before reduce.

2026-03-02 - Security (Mina Chowdhury): Reviewed storage plan. Need KMS-encrypted bucket for customer-sensitive evals. Added requirement and flag in publisher to toggle encrypted publish. Marked security_review_required=true for customer-facing profiles.
2026-03-04 - Marco Ruiz: Added profile-publisher CLI (publish-profile --manifest ...). Publishes manifest + artifacts and returns profile_id. Created smoke CI job: ci/publish-and-rerun-smoke.yaml

2026-03-06 - QA (Evan Park): Smoke CI ran, but re-run metrics differ by 0.8% on BLEU due to float aggregation order in Rust runner. Marco fixed sorter and re-ran; now within 0.03% across 5 reruns. Documented tolerance thresholds in the manifest (metrics_tolerance_pct).

2026-03-08 - Product (Lina Gomez): Reviewed UX for console display of published profiles. Requested adding 'recommended_runtime_pin' and 'fallback_variants' fields to manifest. Added fallback_variants as list in the schema.
next_steps: Finish PR reviews, add KMS bucket wiring, validate large-corpus reservoir adapter at scale, and deploy profile-publisher to staging registry. Coordinate with console team for manifest ingestion API. Plan rollout: opt-in for internal models for 2 weeks, then enable for public catalog entries.
notes_for_hand_off: If reassigning, ensure you have AWS profile write creds and access to harness CI runners. Check the 'manifest v1' schema in the design doc before continuing. Tests: run smoke e2e with sample_size=100 and ensure metrics within manifest.tolerance.
